niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces that feel clean, structured, and visually controlled: light neutral backgrounds with soft purple/gray accents in many general-product screens, clear hierarchy, organized cards or rows, spacious spacing, and reduced clutter. They repeatedly favor concise, streamlined layouts with fewer competing elements, simpler action areas, and readable labeled controls. In some data-dense or code/dashboard contexts, they also show a secondary preference for sleek dark navy themes with cool blue/teal accents, compact floating action surfaces, and refined translucent dark cards. Overall, they like polished modern UI with soft rounding, subtle borders, clear grouping, and strong scanability over noisy, heavy, overly assertive, or awkwardly crowded designs.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers cohesive, polished color systems—most often light neutral backgrounds with soft purple/gray accents and restrained contrast, though in code/dashboard contexts also favors deep navy dark themes with cool blue/teal accents over muddier or harsher dark palettes.
Prefers layouts with balanced breathing room, open spacing, and controlled density; dislikes both cluttered crowded compositions and awkward oversized empty gaps.
Prefers strong, obvious hierarchy with clear titles, sectioning, labeled actions, readable rows/cards, and content that is easy to scan quickly.
Prefers organized, well-grouped layouts such as card-based sections, structured rows, compact grids, and simplified navigation/action placement rather than fragmented or weakly organized screens.

Prefers fewer competing elements, fewer overlays, simpler headers, concise copy, and streamlined controls such as single clear CTAs or compact action groups instead of heavy toolbars, decorative extras, or redundant UI layers.

Prefers polished modern components with subtle borders, soft rounding, pill treatments, refined cards, and lighter or translucent surfaces rather than heavy framed, opaque, or harshly outlined components.

Prefers the amount of visible information to match the task: richer detail and more metrics when it improves utility in dashboards/travel/data views, but concise reduced content in simple forms, loading states, and agreement/entry screens.
